story:
In the middle of the moor, a short walk apart as giants walk, stand Borimo and Trahern, and they have quarrelled since before Rome over which of them stands nearer the Bed. The drovers of the Cornish road have told the quarrel to the clerks of Prydwen Keep for generations, and the clerks have written it down so many times that the roll calls it the old suit, as if it were a case at law that has never come to judgement.

It came to judgement once. In the days of the province a Roman surveyor of the legate's cohort, laying out the province's western bounds, set up his cross-staff on the moor and measured from each giant to the warm ground where the dragon lies, and found Borimo the nearer by a long way, and cut it on a boundary stone, and went home. Borimo has stood a little taller ever since. Trahern has never accepted the measure. The drovers say the stone with the surveyor's cut on it was found broken in pieces the next spring, and the pieces were nearer Trahern.

Borimo is the elder of the two, and the stronger, and the prouder; he holds that standing nearest the Bed is the whole worth of a giant, and that a giant who stands farther off is only rock. He will not suffer a man on his ground, nearer or farther, and comes at any traveller who walks close, as if the man had come to measure him again. In all the years of the old suit neither giant has ever once crossed the moor to help the other. When Borimo is troubled he stands alone, as he has always preferred, and the drovers say Trahern watches from his own ground and is pleased.

When he is broken he does not stay broken. Old Jory Hext, who drove the Cornish road for fifty years, said the moor would not allow it: "the moor keeps its nearest stone." The Hexts walk their cattle wide of him still, and when a new drover asks which way to go round, the old ones ask him first whether he would rather be measured by Borimo or by Trahern.
legend: Borimo is a level 53 named granite giant in the middle of Dartmoor. Despite the old Dartmoor notes, he is aggressive (aggro 200 from the template, range 500); walking near him is a fight, riding past is not. Nothing of his faction stands within 1,200, so he comes alone, and Trahern, 7,000 off, never joins. No spells or styles in the data, just a big giant swinging: a group of fifties, or a strong duo, handles him. Keep the fight in the middle of the moor and away from the Bed to the south-east, where the stonelords and the dragon are. He respawns in about 80 seconds.

loremasterTopic.text: The elder of the two quarrelling giants in the middle of [dartmoor], who holds that standing nearest the Bed is the whole worth of a giant. A Roman surveyor of the old province once measured him the nearer; [trahern] has never accepted it. He suffers no one on his ground, and in all the years of the quarrel neither giant has crossed the moor to help the other.

bookPage: From the roll of Prydwen Keep, a clerk's note in the margin of the drovers' accounts. The old suit again: the Hext drovers say Borimo and Trahern are still at it, and that Borimo has stood up a hand taller since the Roman measured him, and that Trahern has taken to facing the other way. I asked young Hext which way the drovers go round them. He said that depends on whether you would rather be measured by Borimo or Trahern, and that a wise drover would rather not be measured at all, and goes round both, wide, on the side away from the warm ground. I have entered the old suit as undecided. It is the forty-first time.
